Python package installs no longer fail under xcrunner's udocker engine.

## pip when uv fails

The Python executor installs packages into the default image with `uv pip install`. On hosts where xcrunner can only use udocker's Fakechroot mode, such as login nodes that block user namespaces and ptrace, every install of a package not already in the image failed with "Could not persist temporary file … Permission denied (os error 13)". uv persists its cache lock with a raw system call that Fakechroot does not map, so the rename reached the host's `/root`.

The install command now retries the same packages with `python -m pip install --no-cache-dir` into the same target (`--system`, or the Singularity prefix) when uv fails. pip is pure Python, so its file calls go through the C library and work under Fakechroot. Where uv works, nothing changes; where it fails, the install is slower but completes. xcrunner 0.1.8 also gives uv a cache that works under udocker, so the retry is rarely needed there.
